text: HALIFAX, Dec. 4, 1903 - The fishing schooner Annie Laurier, homeward bound from the Banks with a full fare of salt cod, went to pieces on the northwest bar of Sable Island in a heavy sea on Tuesday night. The life-saving crew from the island station launched their surfboat at daybreak and took off nine men who had lashed themselves in the rigging, but the captain and four of the crew were swept overboard during the night. The survivors will be brought to this port by the government steamer when the weather moderates.

text: Air show crash, Abbotsford, August 1987: a vintage fighter failed to pull out of a low pass and hit a field beyond the runway. Pilot killed, no spectators hurt.
label: transport

text: A transit bus and a city streetcar collided at the corner of Main and Hastings in Vancouver during the morning rush on March 18, 1949. The streetcar's front end was crushed and the bus was pushed onto the sidewalk. Twenty-two riders were taken to hospital, most with cuts from broken windows.
label: transport

text: Marine occurrence report, 2 June 1996: a tanker inbound to a refinery at Saint John ran aground on a shoal near Partridge Island after its pilot misjudged the tide-set in poor visibility. A tank was breached and roughly 40 tonnes of light crude escaped into the harbour before the cargo was transferred to a second vessel. Booms were placed across the mouth of the Saint John River. The crew of 27 was not injured. The vessel was refloated on the evening high tide with the help of three tugs.
label: transport

text: Car went off the government wharf at Ste. Anne's Bay, Cape Breton, in a fog, October 1935. Driver and wife drowned.
label: transport

text: On the night of April 26, 1956, a passenger train bound for Prince Rupert ran into a rock slide that had come down across the track in a narrow canyon of the Skeena. The locomotive overturned against the cliff and the baggage car followed it; the engineer and fireman were pinned in the cab and died before they could be cut free. None of the 64 passengers was seriously hurt. They were taken out to Terrace on a work train next morning.
label: transport

text: The Yukon Queen II, a small river ferry, capsized at the Pelly Crossing landing in June 1965 when a loaded truck rolled off its deck. Two men on the ferry drowned.
label: transport

text: KINGSTON, Ont., Oct. 8, 1909 - The barge Elgin, in tow of the steamer Rideau, broke her line in a heavy southwest blow off Nine Mile Point last night and went ashore on the rocks. She is a total loss. Her crew of five was rescued by the steamer's yawl after a hard struggle.
label: transport

text: Fatal collision, Highway 11 south of Cochrane, 3 November 2014: a loaded logging truck lost control on a curve and crossed into the path of a minivan carrying a family of five. Three occupants of the van died; the truck driver and two children were airlifted to Sudbury. OPP closed the highway for ten hours and charged the driver with careless driving.
label: transport

text: A single-engine bush plane carrying a trapper and his family to their winter line went missing on a flight from Fort Smith on October 20, 1958. The aircraft was found by an RCAF Lancaster three weeks later on the frozen shore of a small lake, upside down. The trapper had survived for some days and kept a diary on the wing, but all four were dead when rescuers arrived. The pilot had flown into a snow squall shortly after takeoff and attempted a forced landing.
label: transport

text: Grain carrier settled on the bottom at her berth, Thunder Bay, 1978, after a sea valve was left open during unloading. No injuries.
label: transport

text: A light aircraft crashed into a row of houses in north-end Winnipeg shortly after takeoff from the city airport on 27 July 1983. The pilot and a passenger died, and a woman in one of the houses was badly burned. The fire department kept the flames from spreading to the rest of the block.
label: transport

text: NEWCASTLE, N.B., Jan. 1910 - A sleigh carrying four men across the Miramichi on the ice road broke through near the mouth of a brook where the current keeps the ice thin. The horses went down at once. Two of the men were pulled out by a man who saw the accident from shore, but the others were lost. Their bodies have not been recovered.
label: transport

text: Two loaded freight trains met head-on near Field, B.C., on 11 November 1963, on a single-track section. Both locomotive crews jumped. The wreckage blocked the main line for two days.
label: transport

text: In September 1924, the rum-running motor launch Dolphin was found swamped and abandoned off Pubnico; three men aboard are believed drowned.
label: transport

text: A Department of Transport supply ship carrying fuel and stores to a weather station was beset in pack ice in Hudson Strait in early August 1962 and began to take water after the ice crushed her bow plating. Her crew of 34 worked the pumps for two days before an icebreaker reached her and took off 28 men; the master and a skeleton crew stayed aboard until the ice opened, when the ship was escorted to Churchill with a wooden patch over the hole.
label: transport

text: Fourteen people were hurt in February 2004 when a tour bus rear-ended a line of stopped cars on the Lions Gate Bridge approach in Vancouver.
label: transport

text: QUEBEC, Aug. 17, 1908 - The river steamer Beauport, with 200 excursionists aboard, collided with an ocean freighter in a fog off the Island of Orleans this morning. Her starboard paddle box was carried away and a hole torn in her side above the water line. The passengers were thrown into a panic and several jumped overboard, two of whom drowned. The Beauport reached port under her own steam, followed by the freighter, whose bow was hardly scratched.
label: transport

text: A turboprop airliner on a scheduled flight crashed into a wooded hillside about four kilometres short of the runway at a northern British Columbia airport on 6 March 1972, while attempting an instrument approach in snow and fog. Rescue crews reached the wreck on foot. Of the 39 people aboard, 15 survived, including two flight attendants. The investigation found that the crew had descended below the minimum safe altitude and that an altimeter had been misread.
label: transport

text: Motor vehicle collision, Hwy 16 west of Saskatoon, 2019: semi-trailer and passenger van; two dead, five hurt.
label: transport

text: A Coast Guard hovercraft on a search mission struck a submerged log at high speed off Sea Island, British Columbia, in the autumn of 1981 and lost its forward skirt. The crew of four was not hurt and the craft was towed back to base.
label: transport

text: PORT ARTHUR, Ont., Dec. 1911 - The tug Grayling, which went out to the assistance of a disabled steamer in the bay, ran on a reef in the darkness and sank. Her crew was taken off by a fishing smack. Ice is forming rapidly and it is feared she cannot be raised before spring.
label: transport

text: A Toronto Transportation Commission streetcar struck a truck loaded with steel pipe at the corner of Queen and Spadina on the afternoon of May 10, 1951. The pipe was flung through the front windows of the car and eleven passengers were hurt, two of them gravely. The truck driver was charged with failing to yield.
label: transport

text: A snowplough train left the rails in a slide area of the Rogers Pass in January 1953, injuring two of the crew and blocking the line for a day.
label: transport

text: Investigation report, 31 August 2007: a chartered float plane carrying a pilot and four fishermen struck the water while attempting to land on a glassy lake north of Red Lake, Ontario. The aircraft cartwheeled and sank in about 10 metres of water. Two passengers escaped through a window and were picked up by a boat from a nearby lodge; the pilot and two passengers drowned. The Transportation Safety Board found that glassy-water conditions had made it hard for the pilot to judge his height above the surface.
label: transport

text: A motor coach carrying a church choir from Moncton overturned on a hill near Sussex on the night of September 12, 1948, after its brakes failed on the descent. A woman soprano was killed and twenty others were injured.
label: transport

text: WINNIPEG, Oct. 30, 1902 - An emigrant special from Montreal, carrying three hundred settlers bound for the West, was derailed by a spread rail near Rat Portage yesterday. Two coaches went down an embankment. One child was killed and a dozen passengers injured.
label: transport

text: A passenger in a car was killed and three others hurt when their vehicle was struck by a westbound freight train at an unmarked crossing in rural Manitoba, July 1990.
label: transport

text: Six fishermen lost their lives when the herring seiner Northern Spray capsized in a heavy swell in Hecate Strait on 15 January 1969. The vessel, deep-loaded with a full catch, rolled over as she turned for home, according to the lone survivor, who was picked up from an overturned skiff by a passing freighter after five hours in the water. The seiner had been fishing in winds of 40 knots and was icing on her upper works. Fisheries officers are investigating whether the vessel was overloaded.
label: transport

text: Commuter float plane clipped a moored sailboat while landing in Vancouver Harbour, 2015; no injuries, aircraft towed away.
